newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi welcomes a force to help refugees in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Burundi welcomes a force to help refugees in Zaire.

text.p: Burundian military leader Pierre Buyoya said on Saturday he welcomed military intervention to aid refugees stranded in eastern Zaire but opposed a military force to resolve Burundi's political problems.

"I am in favour of humanitarian action to save the lives of so many refugees who are dying in eastern Zaire, but as we have always said in Burundi we are against military intervention to solve our political problems," Buyoya told reporters.
"The government of Burundi will consider (what to do) if there is a concrete proposal to have military intervention if this for a humanitarian purpose, but not for other means," Buyoya said.

The reaction is the first response of Burundi's leadership, which came to power in a coup d'etat on July 25, to a U.N. proposal to send an international force to assist around a million refugee camps displaced from east Zaire camps.

Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army resisted an East African proposal in June to station peace-keeping troops on its soil, arguing intervention would undermine the army's ability to conduct a war against Hutu rebels.
Regional states imposed sanctions on Burundi six days after the coup and Buyoya warned that Burundi could go the way of eastern Zaire because of the economic and transport blockade.

"The problems in east Zaire could lead to a regional implosion and if the international community continues with the blockade against Burundi then don't be surprised if you also see an implosion here," he said.

More than 100,000 Burundian Hutu refugees are missing after fleeing camps north of east Zaire's Uvira town three weeks ago because of fighting between ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels who together with allies now control much of east Zaire.
Around 150,000 people -- mainly civilians -- have died in three years of civil war in Burundi since the country's first democratically elected Hutu president was murdered in an attempted army coup.
